articles.title: Amy Grant's emotional account of doctors and nurses singing outside Dolly Parton's hospital room
articles.summary: Amy Grant reveals the emotional story of doctors and nurses singing outside Dolly Parton's Vanderbilt Hospital room near the end of her life.
articles.body: Amy Grant shared a touching story from outside Dolly Parton's hospital room. In a new interview with Fox News Digital, the 65-year-old musician opened up about what it meant to her to honor Parton at the 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards, and shared a story she heard from a friend who worked at Vanderbilt Hospital, where Parton died. "Someone in Dolly's close circle had said, 'I know Dolly loves to sing to the tune of 'Amazing Grace,' praise Jesus.' And I said, 'Do you mean praise God? Because that would like be the same syllables,' and she said, 'No praise Jesus and, as a matter of fact, some of the administration, an old and a younger doctor, some of the gathered outside her room toward the end,'" Amy said. "And I'm just trying to imagine, has there ever been a circle of doctors and nurses singing praise Jesus to the tune of 'Amazing Grace' outside anybody's room? I would venture to say no," she added. DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH Parton died on Tuesday, Aug. 25 at the age of 80, following a brief battle with cancer. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Amy shared many memories from her friendship with Parton, noting the singer "always presented at the top of her game" and was always dressed to the nines. Grant joked that she didn't "know who had the behind the scenes look at Dolly, except maybe God." What Amy called, the "magic" of Parton was her kind spirit and how "she was so intentional with the way she reached out to people." She recalled how kind Parton was when meeting her stage manager, and how she offered to send a video to her guitarist's daughter when she found out her and her friends were having a "Dolly Parton night." "She chose to see other people and my feeling is that's the first act of love. Love sees," Amy said. "Then when I saw Dolly, years later, she said, 'How's that magical child of yours?' All I could think of was like, do you take notes?" Amy said. "When she passed, I did think, man, Dolly, I hope all of us think about the intentional choices that you made for how you wanted to live. And I hope we are all reminded of the power of our own choices for how we might live a little differently." The "Lucky One" singer recently honored Parton with a tribute at the 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards, singing alongside Natalie Grant. She explained she initially was only meant to do the spoken introduction, but Natalie and her husband asked her to join in on the song. The 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards took place on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena, hosted by Tauren Wells. Amy described feeling "a lot of emotion with Dolly's passing and to have the opportunity to speak about" her at the award show, noting she "was not able to read through teleprompter one time without getting choked up." articles.title: Trump staffer Britt McHenry escorted from NBA arena after throwing beer at fan
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards opened their much-anticipated NBA season with a win, but Trump staffer Britt McHenry didn’t see it all. McHenry was in attendance for...
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards opened their much-anticipated NBA season with a win, but Trump staffer Britt McHenry didn't see it all.

McHenry was in attendance for the start of the game between the Wizards and Milwaukee Bucks Wednesday night, but the former Fox News and ESPN host was forced to leave Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C., early after a heated incident with fans.

According to Page Six , McHenry and a friend were sitting in front of a group of fans who became loud and obnoxious. After they allegedly began heckling former Wizard and current Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma, McHenry supposedly asked the fans to "ease up," which prompted them to redirect their attention toward her.

A source told Page Six that one of the fans escalated the situation by saying misogynistic things to McHenry before throwing a drink at the current Trump administration press adviser. McHenry retaliated by doing the same thing. Security later arrived to escort McHenry from the stands, allegedly removing the fan who threw a drink at her as well.

The video shows McHenry had a drink thrown at her while leaving the seat, which led the former Fox News host to grab a beverage and toss it back at the fan, spawning a sort of food fight with several items being sent in her direction. But according to one witness who shared the above video, McHenry also threw a burger at a fan before people began recording the incident.

Page Six claims McHenry was escorted out of the arena. Although the video shows her walking out of the arena with security, TMZ reported McHenry wasn't kicked out, alleging she opted to leave while her friend went back to their seats.

ESPN infamously suspended McHenry for one week after she was caught on video berating a tow company employee. She has since claimed the tow truck company's publicly released video was " highly edited" and "highly doctored. "

McHenry has not yet commented on the videos.

articles.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Teaser Falls Flat After Promise of a New Look: ‘That’s It??’
articles.summary: Marvel fans were left underwhelmed after the studio dropped a new teaser for “Avengers: Doomsday” during Game 1 of the World Series, offering only a few glim...
articles.body:
Marvel fans were left underwhelmed after the studio dropped a new teaser for "Avengers: Doomsday" during Game 1 of the World Series, offering only a few glimpses of new footage.

In the sneak peek, Pedro Pascal's Mister Fantastic took the mound for a ceremonial first pitch, before the video cut to commentary from a number of MLB players. The teaser also showed glimpses of Chris Evans' return as Steve Rogers, as well as the destruction to come from Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. Other notable MCU figures spotted in the clip were Chris Hemsworth's Thor, Letitia Wright's Black Panther, Paul Rudd's Ant-Man and Anthony Mackie's Captain America.

There didn't seem to be any big reveals, despite the fact the MLB teased earlier on Thursday that the first Tampa Bay Rays vs. Milwaukee Brewers World Series game would feature " an exclusive preview of 'Avengers: Doomsday,' " indicating there may be something big to tune in for.

Yet, as fans quickly pointed out, the World Series spot seemed to show more of the same, prompting mixed reactions from fans.

"I had to watch 3 innings of f–king BASEBALL for this s–t," wrote one frustrated fan on X. Another chimed in with, "oh so like 3 new seconds lol." A third commented , "All of that just for like 10 seconds of new footage."

A different fan noted , "sooo 1 new scene … barely," while another bluntly wrote , "THAT'S IT???"

However, not everyone was frustrated by the short sneak peek, as others made sure to voice their excitement for the upcoming superhero movie. "I actually like that they're recycling the same scenes," one fan defended . "I don't want them to give too much away like with 'Spider-Man BND.'"

A different fan expressed a similar sentiment, writing , "I honestly am not mad they didn't show more, I want to enjoy every minute in that theatre."

Watch the new teaser for yourself above.

"Avengers: Doomsday," which arrives in theaters on December 18, was written by Michael Waldron and Stephen McFeely and produced by Kevin Feige and the Russos. It will immediately be followed by a sequel, titled "Avengers: Secret Wars," to be released on December 17, 2027.

articles.title: 'Yet more rest needed': Amitabh Bachchan shares health update after social media break
articles.summary: Veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan shared a fresh update on his health, saying he needs more rest as he continues to recover.
articles.body: Veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan shared a fresh update on his health, saying he needs more rest as he continues to recover. The actor posted the message on his Tumblr blog on Friday, a day after announcing a temporary break from online communication following medical advice.Amitabh Bachchan regularly interacts with fans through his blog and social media accounts. "Yet more rest needed .. adjusting .. thinking and wondering .. the human body and its uniqueness," he wrote.Amitabh Bachchan says he is following doctors' adviceThe actor's latest post follows an earlier message in which he apologised to fans for being unable to share regular updates. Amitabh Bachchan explained that doctors instructed him to avoid writing and communicating online for a few days. He is currently following their advice and prioritising rest.Before his latest Tumblr update, Amitabh Bachchan addressed fans on X while extending his Dussehra greetings. He also explained that his doctors placed him under strict instructions to rest and recuperate."First Dussehra greetings to all .. love happiness, fulfilment, prayers. Under very strict rest and recuperation .. so am not allowed to communicate .. do excuse .. my apologies," he wrote.The actor further asked his followers to treat the message as his response for the time being. He expressed hope that he would be able to communicate more regularly later. "But do take this as my respected response .. more hopefully later."Mumbai police investigate reported bomb threat emailThe health update comes amid reports of a bomb threat email allegedly targeting Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow in Mumbai. According to reports, a school in the city's Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) area received the email on Friday.Mumbai Police have launched an investigation into the reported threat. However, it has not been confirmed whether the email specifically named either Jalsa or Prateeksha, the actor's residences in Mumbai. The available information does not establish any connection between the reported threat and Amitabh Bachchan's health update. The police investigation into the email remains ongoing.Amitabh Bachchan's longstanding connection with fansAmitabh Bachchan has used digital platforms for years to share personal reflections and communicate with his audience. He started his personal blog in 2008 and has continued to post updates about his experiences, thoughts and professional activities.Amitabh Bachchan's most recent major film release, according to the information available, was the Tamil-Hindi bilingual action drama 'Vettaiyan'. The film was released in theatres on October 10, 2024. Up next, Big B will be seen in 'Kalki 2'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘What’s with the hate?’: Kriti Sanon reacts to backlash over her Raksha Bandhan ad outfit on Kareena Kapoor's talk show
articles.summary: Kriti Sanon faced heavy trolling on social media in August over her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan ad, with critics calling it “revealing”.
articles.body: Kriti Sanon faced heavy trolling on social media in August over her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan ad, with critics calling it “revealing”. The brand eventually pulled the ad. Speaking to Kareena Kapoor Khan on 'What Women Want', Kriti has now addressed the backlash. She said she generally doesn’t pay attention to trolls, but added, “But this is something that actually happened recently where my choli became the national debate. I couldn’t believe that my choli had become a six-people panel discussion on prime-time news. I was like, ‘What is going on?’”.Kriti Sanon on her choli becoming a ‘national debate’The actress said she was shocked by the intensity of the hate, but felt the issue went beyond her. “I felt that it was not about me; it was a much larger issue, where I felt like women are under scrutiny for everything, and it is only women who get targeted for the smallest thing,” she said, adding, “The amount of hate that happens. What’s with the hate?” Though she usually ignores trolls, Kriti spoke about how nasty people can get. “People who were talking about culture and respect were ironically the ones who were commenting on my parents’ posts and sister’s posts with the nastiest abusive language. They read all these things. What have they done?”.Kriti Sanon on what women actually want“It is important for women to stand up for themselves because I feel like everything is such a question, and who has given this right to these people to be commenting on us, and for what? What women actually want is to not be judged and for people to actually mind their own business," Kriti concluded.Kriti Sanon’s Raksha Bandhan ad rowThe row began when GIVA released its Raksha Bandhan ad starring Kriti Sanon, in which she wears an Indo-Western outfit and ties a rakhi to her brother and her pet dog. Kriti had earlier responded to the backlash on Instagram, questioning why women are still judged by what they wear. “Also, when will we stop telling women what to wear? Ethnic fashion has evolved over the years, yet a woman’s respect for her culture is still measured by her clothes. Culture and traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!”.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Tiger Shroff sells Mumbai apartment for Rs 9 crore days after firing incident near his car in Juhu, third property sale by the actor in about a year
articles.summary: Tiger Shroff has sold an apartment in Mumbai’s Khar West for Rs 9 crore.
articles.body: Tiger Shroff has sold an apartment in Mumbai’s Khar West for Rs 9 crore. As per property registration documents, the deal was registered on October 22, 2026. This is the third property sale by the actor in about a year. Let's learn more about it in detail.Details of the Khar West apartmentAccording to documents shared by real estate data analytics firm CRE Matrix, the flat is on the ninth floor of Rustomjee Paramount D Co-operative Housing Society. It has a carpet area of 1,291.14 sq ft and an exclusive area of 95.80 sq ft. The sale was done at around Rs 64,891 per sq ft. A stamp duty of Rs 54 lakh was paid, and the deal includes two covered car parking spaces.The documents show that Tiger had bought the flat from developer Keystone Realtors Private Limited on July 17, 2018, for Rs 7.61 crore. He took possession on November 30, 2019. The actor could not be reached for comment.The sale comes soon after Tiger made headlines for a scary incident. On the evening of October 18, at least two men opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area and then fled on a motorcycle. Tiger escaped relatively unhurt, but his driver and a bystander were injured.Earlier sale in the same projectAbout a year ago, Tiger Shroff sold another flat in the same project for Rs 15.6 crore, as per documents reviewed by Square Yards. He made a gain of nearly 31% on the deal.That apartment was on the 22nd floor and had a carpet area of 1,989.72 sq ft and a built-up area of 2,189 sq ft. He had bought it in 2018 for Rs 11.62 crore. It came with three car parking spaces. The buyer paid a stamp duty of Rs 93.60 lakh and registration charges of Rs 30,000.Rustomjee Paramount is spread over 1.65 acres and offers two, three, four and five-bedroom apartments, according to Square Yards.Pune property sold earlier this yearEarlier in 2026, the actor also sold a residential property in Pune’s Hadapsar for Rs 8.87 crore, according to property registration documents accessed by Zapkey. He had bought it in March 2024 for Rs 7.5 crore, which gives a gross return on investment of 18.3%, Zapkey said.The apartment is in the Yoo Pune building by Panchshil Realty and was sold along with three parking spaces. It measures 4,249 sq ft and was sold at Rs 20,891 per sq ft. The deal was registered on March 31, 2026, with a stamp duty of over Rs 62 lakh and a registration fee of Rs 30,000.Tiger Shroff is known for his action roles and dancing skills. The son of veteran actor Jackie Shroff, he made his acting debut in 2014 with ‘Heropanti’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Hollywood actor Jason Momoa has purchased the former estate of Sam Neill in New Zealand's Central Otago region for NZD 15 million. This expansive property features stunning mountain views and has a rich history, including its past use for government horticultural research.
articles.body: Hollywood star Jason Momoa has officially put down permanent roots in New Zealand’s South Island. According to recent reports, the beloved actor officially acquired Sam Neill’s former Queensland property located in New Zealand following his death. The ownership of the estate had been earlier transferred to his ex-wife, Noriko Watanabe, and now, Momoa has bought out the grand estate. Here’s a look into the iconic home.Jason Momoa buys out Sam Neill’s former New Zealand estateAccording to reports from Realtor.com, the beloved actor bought the ‘Jurassic Park’ actor’s property earlier this year in September. He spent a whopping NZD 15 million on the property, which is overall NZD 3.5 million above the official rating valuation. The estate is situated in the rural enclave of Dalefield, near Queenstown in New Zealand's Central Otago region, a famous area that is known for mountain landscapes and large residential holdings.OneRoof also reported that this transaction marks the second-highest residential sale in the Queenstown-Lakes district in 2026, trailing only behind a luxury lodge on Mooney Road in Speargrass Flat that had earlier sold for NZD 16.5 million.More about Sam Neill’s former Queensland propertySir Sam Neill bought the space in 1999 and owned the property until it was transferred into his ex-wife’s name. The main residential structures on the property were designed by New Zealand architect Richard Naish. Other than that, the main central living house alongside a dedicated "Clubhouse" has been built for hosting and social gatherings there. As for the overall aesthetic of the property, the structures reflect a rural Central Otago alpine aesthetic and have integrated natural elements like timber finishing, stone, and large framed windows designed to capture panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and farm landscape.As for its history, even before the ‘Jurassic Park’ star was bought, the estate had been used for government horticultural research. Remnants of those experimental plantings still remain on the property. Since the space is so vast, it includes organic Pinot Noir and Riesling grapevines as part of the broader Two Paddocks vineyard network, alongside organic vegetable gardens, fruit orchards, and lavender fields used for essential oil production. articles.title: Quentin Tarantino Surprises Fans With 17 Minutes of ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ at AFI Fest
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino surprised audiences on Friday night at AFI Fest when he shared the first 17 minutes of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.” Taranti...
articles.body:
Quentin Tarantino surprised audiences on Friday night at AFI Fest when he shared the first 17 minutes of "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth."

Tarantino made a special appearance at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Hollywood, following a screening of "Once Upon a Time … In Hollywood." Following the Q&A moderated by Rotten Tomatoes' Jacqueline Coley, the filmmaker said, "Well, I could talk a little bit about 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,' or I could show you the first 17 minutes."

Directed by David Fincher , who was also in attendance, the film sees the return of Cliff Booth played by Brad Pitt. The film picks up in 1977 from the original film's 1969 timeline. The logline reads: "Los Angeles no longer needs a hippie-slaying stuntman the way it did. But Hollywood will always have problems, problems that can only be solved by someone with Cliff's unique (occasionally extralegal) abilities. When he's not earning his keep bartending or as a projectionist, Cliff Booth is a fixer — solving situations for Hollywood's great and, sometimes, not so good."

During the Q&A, Tarantino, who wrote the screenplay, shared his decision to revisit Cliff Booth. He said, "I tend to not remember good reviews of mine in quotes; I remember the bad reviews in quotes, but I don't really remember good reviews of mine in quotes. But one quote that I do remember somebody writing about 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood' was, 'This seems like the first world Quentin Tarantino has ever created that he would like to live in,' and there is that aspect; I loved the Cliff Booth character," Tarantino said. "I loved the way that Brad played him, and there was this aspect of him as sort of like a paperback hero. I could see like a series of paperbacks with Cliff Booth getting involved with this adventure or that adventure or something like that."

The Netflix film is set to premiere in Imax theaters on Nov. 25, before hitting the streamer Dec. 23.

He also talked about his upcoming play "The Popinjay Cavalier ," which stars Sacha Baron Cohen and is set to premiere in London's West End next year. "I'm not going to talk a whole lot about that, but our previews are in February. In November we'll start rehearsals." He went on to say, "I'm just a writer, and that's just kind of what I do. I'm always writing."

articles.title: Quote of the day by Jennifer Aniston: ‘I'm still a romantic. I still believe in love,’ a reminder to never lose faith in love
articles.summary: Jennifer Aniston shares her heartfelt belief in love despite heartbreak, encouraging others to embrace love and healing after relationships. Discover insights on love and moving forward.
articles.body: There's a strange thing about heartbreak. You can spend weeks telling yourself that you're fine, get on with your work, meet your friends and barely think about the person. Then a song comes on, or you walk past a place you used to visit together, and suddenly you're remembering things you thought you'd moved past. Healing doesn't always happen in a straight line, no matter how much you'd like it to.For some people, the hardest part isn't getting over a relationship. It's finding the courage to let someone new into their lives afterwards. The thought of starting again can be exciting, but it can also be frightening when you know how badly things can hurt.Today's quote of the day by Jennifer Aniston is: “I'm still a romantic. I still believe in love.”What does Jennifer Aniston's quote mean?Aniston said this in an interview with Harper's Bazaar Australia. When she was asked if her past relationships had changed the way she felt about love, her answer was clear: she still believed in it.It's easy to say you believe in love when things are going well. But when you break up, you start thinking about what went wrong. Trusting someone new seems like a task, as you are afraid of going through the same pain and betrayal. The ghosts of the past haunt your present and lurk over the future.Sometimes, you become more cautious without even realising it. A new person might seem lovely, but you're already wondering when things will go wrong. You might avoid getting attached because, in your mind, not caring too much means you can't get hurt too badly.The trouble is that protecting yourself from every possible disappointment can also keep you from getting close to anyone. That doesn't mean you should ignore your instincts or trust people before they've earned it. It simply means that one person's actions don't have to become the standard by which you judge everyone else.Why does Jennifer Aniston's message still matter today?People are often quick to tell someone who is heartbroken to move on. They might say there are plenty of other people out there or that the breakup happened for a reason. Sometimes those words help. Other times, you just want someone to understand that you're not ready to stop missing the person yet.There's no fixed schedule for getting over someone. You might feel better after a few weeks, or you might need considerably longer. You can know that ending the relationship was the right decision and still feel sad about it. Those two things aren't mutually exclusive.Then comes the question of dating again. Friends might encourage you to put yourself out there, but only you know when you're ready. There's nothing wrong with enjoying your own company for a while, rediscovering old interests or getting comfortable with life as it is now.Being single doesn't have to be a waiting period before your next relationship. It can just be a part of your life in its own right.At the same time, it's worth remembering that a new relationship won't necessarily repeat the old one. The person will be different, the circumstances will be different, and you'll probably be a little different yourself. You may have a clearer idea of what you need from a partner, which behaviours you're no longer willing to accept and where you need to communicate better.That doesn't mean you should enter a relationship expecting everything to work out. Real relationships are rarely that tidy. People have disagreements, misunderstand each other and occasionally say the wrong thing.Jennifer Aniston's early lifeJennifer Aniston was born on 11 February 1969 in Sherman Oaks, California. Acting was familiar to her from an early age, as her father, John Aniston, also worked in the industry. He became widely known for playing Victor Kiriakis in the television soap opera 'Days of Our Lives'.Aniston attended Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School of Music & Art and Performing Arts in New York City, where she studied acting. But having an interest in the profession and a parent who understood the industry didn't mean her own career would automatically take off.She spent her early years taking smaller roles and looking for opportunities. The success most people associate with her name was still ahead of her.How did Jennifer Aniston rise to fame?In 1994, Jennifer Aniston landed one of the most iconic roles of her career. She played Rachel Green in 'Friends,' the sitcom which became a major success, and her character soon became one of television's most recognisable personalities. Viewers followed her friendships, romances and career struggles, while her hairstyle became a trend of its own.The role changed Aniston's career, but she didn't stop working in television and film once the sitcom ended in 2004. She appeared in movies such as 'Bruce Almighty', 'The Break-Up' and 'Marley & Me'. Later, she returned to television with 'The Morning Show'. It also starred Reese Witherspoon.Her personal life has also attracted plenty of public attention, particularly her relationships. Celebrities may have millions of people following their lives, but when a relationship ends, they go through many of the same feelings as everyone else.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: The Surprise Guest in ‘You Can See Everything’ Could Win an Oscar. Should They?
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “You Can See Everything,” now playing in theaters. The question that’s consumed the awards-pundit class sin...
articles.body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for "You Can See Everything," now playing in theaters.

The question that's consumed the awards-pundit class since "You Can See Everything" exploded into theaters last week is whether Amanda Seyfried, the unlikely linchpin of this hybrid documentary, can be nominated for or win an acting Oscar. A24 is planning to campaign her for one. Much of her time onscreen is as herself, reacting in real time — but she does, eventually, re-enact co-director Nathan Fielder's remembered interactions with disgraced tech founder Elizabeth Holmes.

In this, she's reprising a role that, with the 2022 Hulu series "The Dropout," already won her an Emmy and a Golden Globe. It's the role, now that "You Can See Everything" is on track to become one of the most financially successful documentaries in history, that's become Seyfried's signature. To this viewer, the question is at once an amusing thought experiment ( sure, why not? ), and a testament to Seyfried's compelling screen presence — and more than a little beside the point. For once, an Oscar seems minimizing. What Seyfried's doing in her most compelling screen work ever is something other, or more, than simply acting.

To be clear, the parts of "You Can See Everything" when she is literally acting are riveting on their own terms. Seyfried simply wears the role of Holmes easily. She's doubly disadvantaged — in that we've just spent 90 minutes with the real Holmes, against whom we can compare Seyfried, and in that we've also spent time absorbing just how little Seyfried understands the enigma of Holmes' motivations. And yet Seyfried somehow creates a coherent and compelling version of a woman we don't understand, and we know she doesn't, really, either.

To pigeonhole Seyfried's appearance in "You Can See Everything" as, solely, an acting performance misses the rawness of Seyfried's presence here. She allows herself to be seen thinking through a conundrum, as herself, and falling short of finding answers — in other words, after Holmes and husband Billy Evans, she's the documentary's other subject. Seyfried delivers a painful and unresolved excavation of the mind of an actor, seeming to land in a place of uncertainty as to how her own past work as Holmes has changed the story even as she willingly takes on the part once more.

Consider, for instance, the scene in which Seyfried visits Evans at home, after Holmes' incarceration. This is impressively game and daring. And Seyfried is, I suppose, "acting," both in the theorist's sense that all of us are acting our way through life and in the particular that Seyfried has set out to lure information out of Evans to better understand the seemingly bizarre arrangement Fielder and co-director Lance Oppenheim had been excavating before Holmes went to prison. But is she acting, in the traditional sense, when she meets and interacts with Holmes and Evans' two children, or when she defends her social media post criticizing the late Charlie Kirk against Evans' mockery? Alternately tender and outraged, Seyfried allows us into her world, just as Holmes tried to. But Holmes, talking past real questioning, couldn't get there, no matter how all-access her invitation to Fielder had been. Seyfried, by contrast, seems deeply in touch with emotions lying just under the surface. And her increasing befuddlement both matches our own and raises the question of just how deeply an actor can ever understand their subject.

Seyfried, just as Holmes and Evans do in their askew manner, knows her angles. It wasn't lost on me that within the frame as Fielder speaks to her at her home is a miniature playhouse, of the sort her company Make It Cute sells. That the computer on which she and Fielder watch video of Holmes watching "The Dropout" is propped on coffee table books about Seyfried's great passion, dogs, and that she and Fielder discuss Holmes while feeding her photogenic horses on her photogenic farm only burnish her brand further. And yet she cannot help but exposing more than she may mean to.

A conversation about the ethics of "The Dropout" — a drama based on real events that, as with any dramatization, used creative license, and that many viewers took as fact — places Seyfried in a surprisingly exposed position. Holmes did not, literally, say and do all the things that Seyfried says and does in the role, Seyfried admits, but she may well have, and the performance overall conjures the sense of a person who is unconcerned with scientific accuracy or with the truth. Shouldn't that be enough? "I didn't do that to her," Seyfried concludes, after attempting to walk herself through a justification of "The Dropout" as plainly not depicting objective reality, no matter what viewers think. "She did that to herself." She seems to be convincing herself not to feel guilty, up until her final line, delivered with a "It's Chinatown"-style futility. "It's very complicated," she says, having indulged the complications long enough.

Coming into "You Can See Everything," this viewer saw Elizabeth Holmes' Theranos as transparently fraudulent and "The Dropout" as an excellent TV show that was in no need of moral justification. Leaving the theater, nothing about those beliefs had changed, but engaging the question of what Seyfried might have owed to Holmes allowed both women to be seen in intriguing new lights. Seyfried, painfully aware of the existence of the two young children she'd met, twists around the question of whether her past work might have been unfair, or have been presented as possessed of a truth its creators didn't actually know. And in this moment, she seems less to be acting than to be, in a moment of painful frankness I admire her for allowing herself to experience on-camera, acted upon.

Say this much: "You Can See Everything" is undeniably a career high for an actor who has seemed at times in her career like an underdog. (A sliding-doors scenario for the ages: The role of Elizabeth Holmes originally went to sketch comedian Kate McKinnon, and Seyfried got the role only after McKinnon dropped out and Seyfried got a career-boosting Oscar nomination for 2020's "Mank.") Amiably loopy in interviews — including in red-carpet appearances at this year's Academy Museum Gala, where Seyfried sidestepped discussing the film in favor of free-associative Dada — and impressively shifting between genres to avoid being pigeonholed, Seyfried is easy to root for, but can seem hard to know.

Which makes the Oscar talk make perfect sense. Seyfried has gone to a very raw place in "You Can See Everything" — and, not for nothing, has delivered some of the most memorable humor in its second half. (Her growing scandalization at Evans' control over Holmes' image and her life allows the viewer a compelling way to stay engaged with the story once Holmes herself leaves it.) But whether or not she can break through in what would, despite vaguely similar precedent — Maria Bakalova in the 2020 "Borat" sequel was nominated for reacting against real life — be close to an unprecedented case, Seyfried has done something more impressive than earning any award. She's opened up her work as an actor — both her preparation and the moral question of what it means to play a living person — to careful scrutiny, and was vulnerable enough to attempt to talk it through, and to be shown to be uncertain. This appearance, or performance, or whatever, will be discussed far beyond Oscar season. It situates Seyfried as what we ought to have known she was all along: Among the most daring stars of her generation.

articles.title: F1 United States GP: Lewis Hamilton pips Max Verstappen in FP3
articles.summary: Ferrari heads into qualifying having topped every practice session at COTA
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton finished final practice on top at Formula 1's United States Grand Prix, leading Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc into qualifying at Austin.

Hamilton was the only driver to break the 1m35s barrier in the final 20 minutes of third practice, as frequent track limits transgressions kept Ferrari team-mate Leclerc from leapfrogging him on the leaderboard.

Following an opening quarter of the session which can only be described as pedestrian, action picked up as Hamilton set a 1m36.716s on softs to get ahead of a number of medium-tyred install laps.

His time was soon beaten by Liam Lawson in the Racing Bulls and McLaren's Oscar Piastri , while several heavy hitters kept turning laps on medium tyres instead.

Verstappen even went top courtesy of a 1m35.702s on the yellow sidewall tyre, despite recurring complaints about his unsettling downshifts.

Hamilton swiftly improved upon the Dutchman's lap, using softs to set a 1m35.561s. But when Leclerc took over command with a 1m35.127s despite using the slower mediums, that underlined there was still a lot more pace to find.

Entering the final 20 minutes, Antonelli took a tenth out of Leclerc's time on softs, but his lap was scratched for breaking track limits at Turn 9.

Verstappen did adhere to the white lines to set a 1m35.061s and go top, with Red Bull the quickest car through sector one, only for Hamilton to dip below the 1m35s barrier with a 1m34.893s.

Track limits, which have been a recurring theme throughout practice, also kept Leclerc from reclaiming first as he dipped over the white line at Turn 10.

That meant the Monegasque had to settle for third behind Hamilton and Verstappen, setting up a finely poised qualifying session on Saturday afternoon.

Championship leader Antonelli was fourth ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell , as the Silver Arrows appears to be a half-step behind on pure pace, with Piastri sixth in the difficult to tame MCL40.

In the Audi , Nico Hulkenberg kept McLaren 's Lando Norris from seventh, with the world champion's 1m35.2s also deleted for track limits at Turn 10.

Alpine driver Pierre Gasly was ninth, a full second behind Hamilton, with Isack Hadjar 10th in the second Red Bull as the Frenchman was left frustrated by his car's handling.

articles.title: Gasperini: ‘Roma felt we could win, 3-3 at Napoli a positive confidence booster’
articles.summary: Gian Piero Gasperini insists Roma ‘felt we could win’ the game with Napoli even after going 3-2 down, and is ultimately satisfied with a 3-3 draw. ‘It’s anot...
articles.body:
Gian Piero Gasperini insists Roma 'felt we could win' the game with Napoli even after going 3-2 down, and is ultimately satisfied with a 3-3 draw . 'It's another positive confidence booster.'

The Giallorossi showed they refused to give up after going 2-0 down at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona to an acrobatic Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa bicycle kick and Scott McTominay header.

They scored twice in five minutes with Matias Soulé and Leonardo Balerdi to claw it back, only to go behind again to a McTominay strike from outside the box.

There was one final twist as Balerdi nodded in a Wesley cross at the back post for the 3-3 draw at the 89 th minute.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Gian Piero Gasperini AS Roma head coach during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

"Apart from the first half-hour, where Napoli were superior and we struggled playing out from the back, we already started to do better towards half-time and then in the second half it was wide open with many chances," Gasperini told DAZN Italia.

"We felt that we could win the game, so that third Napoli goal could've destroyed us, but instead we got back on track and felt this great conviction we could bring home three points.

"The lads were not frenetic, they didn't panic, we maintained our positions and our style of football. The goals came from quality football too, we had fresh energy with Balerdi, Molina and the others who came off the bench.

"I want to single out Soulé, who had an extraordinary performance, as did Ndicka and others. We are in a great moment of form, we have real self-belief, we play good football, and after this game we really feel as if we've dropped two points, even though considering we were 3-2 down, we'll take it."

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Gian Piero Gasperini, AS Roma head coach, reacts during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Roma have drawn their three biggest games in Serie A so far this season, 2-2 with Inter, 0-0 at Como when down to 10 men, and now 3-3 away to Napoli.

"They are all very different matches, but in all three we felt that we were very competitive with the best in the league," noted Gasperini.

"We came close to beating Inter, even if they recovered two goals, while with Como we were down to 10 men for practically the entire second half, but in the first half were positive. Today, considering the quality of Napoli, having come back to get the result was another positive confidence booster for us."

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Matias Soule of AS Roma celebrates after scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Balerdi was a very late signing for Roma in the summer and he popped up with two goals today.

"There is no doubt that Balerdi and De Roon were leaders and captains at their clubs, their support has been extraordinary. They settled in very quickly, it was easier with De Roon because I worked with him for so many years, but Balerdi knows football, understood the defensive movements very quickly, he has remarkable energy and today scored two goals. A great reinforcement," added Gasperini.

"Napoli won the Scudetto twice in the last few years, so if you are competitive against them, it gives you the strength and confidence to fight it out with anyone."

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Gian Piero Gasperini AS Roma head coach greets Massimiliano Allegri SSC Napoli head coach before the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Gasperini and Max Allegri are great friends, so did the Roma coach run into his Napoli counterpart after that red card on the touchline?

"No. I hope he wasn't angry with me, I wasn't the one who sent him off!" smiled Gasp.

articles.body: Halloween season is upon us, and since the LSU Tigers have a bye next week, it's time for the team's mascot, Mike the Tiger, to bust out his costume. And what better way to celebrate Halloween ahead of Saturday's game against the Auburn Tigers than by dressing as Haddonfield, Illinois' favorite son (actually, maybe he's not the favorite), Michael Myers. And when dressed as Michael Myers, what better way to get in the spirit than by creepily stalking an on-field official just like the star of the "Halloween" franchise (except the third one) did? KANSAS STATE WILDCATS' MASCOT FORCED TO COMPLETE ABSURD AMOUNT OF PUSH-UPS DURING 71-3 VICTORY What a moment. There's so much happening here. The phrase "the European mind cannot comprehend" gets thrown around a lot these days, but I'm a red-blooded American, and it still took me a few moments to process everything that happened in that clip. First of all, you've got a guy in a costume of a tiger, inside of a costume of a guy, who is technically wearing a costume, that costume being — fun fact — a William Shatner mask painted white with the hair teased out. It's costume-ception. FORMER NFL QB SEAN SALISBURY WANTS OFFICIALS TO FACE POSTGAME QUESTIONS JUST LIKE PLAYERS AND COACHES Then stalking the official like he's Laurie Strode is a real choice. articles.title: Maringá are 2026 Série C champions
articles.summary: Maringá won the 2026 Série C titleCredit: Rafael Ribeiro/CBFMaringá defeated Ferroviária 2–1 this Saturday (24) to win the 2026 Brasileirão Série C at Arena...
articles.body:
Maringá won the 2026 Série C title Credit: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

Maringá defeated Ferroviária 2–1 this Saturday (24) to win the 2026 Brasileirão Série C at Arena Fonte Luminosa in Araraquara, São Paulo. Playing away from home, the team scored through Lucas Bonifácio and Ronald Camarão to become champions of the competition's 36th edition.

Despite the presence of 11,500 home fans, the Paraná side were not intimidated by the pressure, especially early in the match. They built their lead within ten minutes and secured the victory.

The São Paulo side went on the attack, needing a win after a 1–1 draw in the first leg. They created chances to break through Dogão's defense but were thwarted by a strong performance from Maringá goalkeeper Guilherme Neto. Denílson pulled one back late in the second half, but they could not find an equalizer to take the final to penalties.

The 2026 Série C championship was Maringá's first national title in their 16-year history.

Maringá fans celebrated at Arena Fonte Luminosa Credit: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

Maringá opened the scoring just three minutes in. The goal came after Caíque Calito broke away at pace and had his shot deflected for a corner. Negueba took the corner, Ronald headed it on, and Lucas Bonifácio fired into the net.

Caíque Calito again threatened the opposition defense and passed to Adeílson, who was unmarked in the box and facing goal but shot over the bar. It was a huge chance wasted by the Paraná side.

That miss could have proved even more painful for Maringá when Ferroviária were awarded a penalty for a foul on Ricardinho. The decision, however, was overturned after a VAR review.

After nearly seeing the hosts equalize, Dogão extended their lead. Ronald Camarão, who scored in the first leg, made the difference once again. He met Jhow's cross in the six-yard box and simply had to tap it into the net.

Lucas Bonifácio opened the scoring for Maringá in the second leg of the Série C final Credit: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

Trailing 2–0, Ferroviária pushed forward and left gaps at the back. In the 21st minute, Zé Vitor surged forward from midfield but was dispossessed by Caíque Calito. Calito launched a counterattack and played the ball into the box. Adeílson cleverly dummied it, allowing the ball to reach Lucas Bonifácio, who hit the post.

Unhappy with his team's performance, Ferroviária coach Rogério Corrêa made two changes before the half-hour mark. Ricardinho and Carlão came off for Arthur Schilling and Guilherme Ferreira, respectively.

The changes paid off. In the 32nd minute, Maringá's Ronald nearly scored an own goal while trying to clear a cross. Two minutes later, Vitor Barreto was in the six-yard box, ready to pull one back, when Thiago Rosa stepped in to clear. In the 40th minute, Vitor Barreto exchanged passes with Juninho before shooting straight at goalkeeper Guilherme Neto.

Maringá and Ferroviária contested the 2026 Série C title Credit: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

In stoppage time, Locomotiva continued to search for a goal. Albano's header forced a good save from Guilherme Neto, who also kept out a header from Guilherme Ferreira. Despite their repeated chances, the hosts went into halftime trailing 2–0, with chants of "Let's turn it around, AFE!" ringing out.

Coach Ivan Campanari's halftime talk with the Maringá players brought a change in approach after the team had come under pressure late in the first half. Two minutes after the restart, Adeílson Maranhão fired over from inside the six-yard box, nearly scoring Ferroviária's third goal. In the 12th minute, Edison Negueba found space to shoot from outside the box and forced a fine save from Dênis Junior.

After twenty minutes of alternating possession with no major scoring chances, Ferroviária brought the final back to life. Denilson received a pass from Fau and pulled one back for the hosts with a fine strike. The Locomotiva fans responded with chants of "I believe."

In stoppage time, Ferroviária threatened Maringá's defense with free kicks near the box, taken by Lucas Rodrigues and Albano, and dangerous crosses. Adeílson and Gabriel Souza showed that the Paraná side would not surrender the title. Full time: Ferroviária 1–2 Maringá.

Congratulations, Maringá, 2026 Série C champions!

articles.title: Mercedes' Antonelli claim pole position for F1 US Grand Prix
articles.summary: Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed pole position on Saturday for the United States Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver clocked the fastest ti...
articles.body:
Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed pole position on Saturday for the United States Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver clocked the fastest time of 1 minute 34.035 seconds in his first flying lap of the final block of qualifying and nobody was able to beat that time in the second run.

Max Verstappen 0.179 seconds behind in second, followed by Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar, who was 0.215 seconds off the pace.

Ferrari disappointed after claiming top spot in all practice sessions and were fourth and fifth with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton respectively.

George Russell in the other Mercedes was sixth, followed by the McLaren duo of Oscar Piastri and defending champion Lando Norris.

Antonelli could claim the drivers' title this weekend and become F1's youngest ever champion at 20 years old. However, his chances of doing so on Sunday are unlikely, especially after the resurgent Verstappen won the last two races in Malaysia and Singapore.

He would need to win the race and for Russell to be not better than ninth and Hamilton not better than fifth.

But it's a matter of time until Antonelli can celebrate his maiden F1 crown as he holds a 102-point lead over Russell with six races to go.

Four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel, now retired, is currently the youngest F1 champion. He won his first title at 23 years, 134 days in 2010.

articles.title: Antonelli takes US pole on weekend he can win title
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli secures pole position for the United States Grand Prix on the weekend on which he can potentially clinch his first world title.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli took pole position for the United States Grand Prix on the weekend on which he can potentially clinch his first world title.

The Mercedes driver beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen by 0.179 seconds, with the Dutchman's team-mate Isack Hadjar third ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton.

Antonelli whooped with delight as he took his first pole position since the Belgian Grand Prix in July and said: "It feels good to be back."

The 20-year-old Italian will become world champion on Sunday if he wins the race with Hamilton lower than fourth and Russell lower than eighth.

Hamilton is already below that position having qualified fifth, while Russell will start sixth ahead of the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris.

Antonelli's pole came as something of a surprise after the Ferraris had topped all three practice sessions and Verstappen had looked strong through the second part of qualifying.

"I wasn't expecting that," said Antonelli's engineer Peter Bonnington, emphasising that his charge's first lap in final qualifying was good enough for pole.

Verstappen had been fourth quickest in Q2 despite being on used tyres but he found his car lacked the requisite grip in the final session.

Antonelli said: "We got pole so we will try to win tomorrow but Max has been very quick and Isack did an incredible job so it is not going to be easy.

"We try to get a good start and hopefully lead into Turn One and try to set the pace, even though it's going to be very tight."

Verstappen said: "Q3 was not good, Q1, Q2 were nice but for whatever reason in run one and two just didn't have a nice balance. No mistakes, just not enough grip. But if it's still a P2, I take it."

Hadjar was just 0.036secs behind the four-time champion while the Ferraris faded when it mattered, as they have so many times this season.

Leclerc, fastest in second and third practice, was 0.232secs off the pace and pipped Hamilton by just 0.044secs.

Russell was 0.441secs off his team-mate while the fastest McLaren was 0.768secs from pole despite an upgrade for this weekend as Norris' best lap time was deleted for breaching track limits.

The Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson took ninth and 10th places but the Briton will be demoted five places because of a penalty for using too many engine parts.

articles.title: Music streaming: Why we're listening to so many old songs
articles.summary: The chart is full is full of old music and classic songs are dominating streaming services. But why?
articles.body:
More music is being created than at any other time in human history. Every day, more than 100,000 songs are being submitted to streaming services.

And despite the deluge of AI music - Spotify says it has removed 75 million "spammy tracks" from its catalogue - real music still makes up most of our listening. The streaming service Deezer says AI accounts for just 0.5% of streams on its platform.

The problem for all those artists creating new music is that our listening habits increasingly show a love for nostalgia.

Luminate, an independent entertainment data and analytics company that tracks music, film, and television consumption first started tracking music streaming in 2008.

This year, it recorded that the streaming of current music (released less than 18 months ago) was significantly dwarfed by older music in both the UK and US.

In the first half of 2026, almost two thirds of the music played (about 60%) was released five or more years ago.

So, if we're stuck in a streaming rut, what's to blame?

In the UK, most of us seem to be shunning new songs.

Eighteen of the year's top 20 bestselling songs were released 12 months ago, or earlier.

The year's eighth biggest hit is Zara Larsson's Lush Life, which originally came out in June 2015. Michael Jackson's Billie Jean (1983) is in 22nd place. Fleetwood Mac's Dreams (1977) is 30th.

It's a sign that, with practically every song ever recorded available at the press of a button, people are increasingly seeking out the classics - or what the music industry categorises as "deep catalogue".

There, in the two most-played genres, R&B and Hip-Hop , about 60% of streams are old-school catalogue hits.

A 'drought' of new music in the UK Charts?

Even when current songs do break out, they themselves dominate streaming for weeks and even months.

Sam Fender and Olivia Dean's duet Rein Me In recently made UK chart history , spending a record-breaking 23 non-consecutive weeks at number one.

Likewise, in America, Ella Langley's Choosin' Texas has become the longest-running number one in US chart history.

The reality, of course, is that hits need to achieve " millions of streams a day " to reach the top of the charts.

But according to the UK's Competition and Markets Authority, nearly two thirds of streams are of music recorded by " only the top 0.4% of artists ".

As we increasingly cling on to our favourites, aspiring artists may be suffering.

Even after a song has gone viral, some musicians say it can be hard to promote subsequent releases and sustain a career. A platform like TikTok isn't set up to boost artists, it's there to create viral moments around a single song.

"It's easier [today] for folks to be passive fans," noted J Erving, the founder of Raye's distribution company, Human Re Sources, in a recent interview with Billboard .

"For you to consider yourself broken [as a mainstream artist], people need to care about you beyond the song. Where is the connectivity? Are people really dialled in in a deeper way?"

It's a problem the music industry is keen to tackle.

Oliver Schusser, the Head of Apple Music, says his streaming service is working to champion "tomorrow's artists" in its curation.

"You know, we do the Super Bowl halftime show, we need to make sure that we still have performers in 10, 20, 30 years," he tells BBC News.

"Because if you look back at the performers we had in the last four years, they all started somewhere before they got to the world's biggest stage."

Other organisations like Sofar Sounds work exclusively with grassroots musicians, putting on intimate pop-up gigs in cities across the globe.

This October, its Shoreditch Sofar Fringe festival showcased a whole host of artists like East London rapper J Casa.

In an age of content oversaturation, Casa thinks there's something unique about a live performance.

Rather than hearing more of what they already know, Casa says audiences form "a lasting connection" with a new artist and their music.

Sofar is also launching its Human Discovery Movement campaign that aims to put music curation and discovery "back into human hands."

Music lovers can now text a "mystery number" and receive voice notes from Sofar's tastemakers with recommendations for new music worldwide.

Are streaming platforms preaching to the choir?

Artificial intelligence (AI) may also be playing its part in the so-called death of new music.

Spotify, and its competitors like Apple Music and Amazon Music, are driving the trend in AI-assisted curation, allowing premium subscribers to automatically generate playlists through text prompts to fit a mood, vibe or occasion.

Musicologist Anna-Kaisa Kaila thinks "there absolutely is potential for bias" with AI-generative playlist technology.

"With AI systems, the bias can either come from the data or from the system itself. If there's not enough training data in a particular style that is perhaps not so commercially dominant, it will be that much harder for the system to pull up tracks in that style."

Others fear an algorithmic streaming bubble is to the detriment of genuine music, its discovery and creatives' livelihoods.

As Tim Garcia, London-based DJ and curator puts it: "They're based on everyone's listening behaviour and data, right? So, you're probably going to get given a very similar recommendation to an artist you're already listening to."

Dan Mackta, managing director at Qobuz, an online music platform that maintains a strict human-first approach to curation, agrees the technology "is never going to want to throw a curve ball at you".

Chiminyo, a London-based independent artist, believes that auto-generated playlists are also misleading people into thinking they're listening to "hand-picked" tunes from bona fide artists - as opposed to digitally mass-produced sound-alikes created to catch streams.

Scrolling through a "relaxing jazz piano playlist" with over 370,000 saves on Spotify, he spots that top featured artists that rack up hundreds of thousands of monthly listens have unverified accounts.

Little - if anything - can be found about them online, he says.

To his trained ear, Chiminyo also says the different artists' tracks sound near identical, reason enough to conclude the compositions have been synthetically mass-produced.

"Its all the same: the same piano feel, the same microphone placement, the same tape machine, has been used on every single one of these tracks."

When asked, Spotify said it had rolled out platform-wide policies against impersonation and is working to the improve filtering out of AI-related issues on its platform. But it acknowledges AI's use in music production sits on a spectrum with some artists choosing to use it to varying degrees.

New music may not be dying out, but it's clear it has a lot to contend with in 2026.

articles.title: Nome da cena indie carioca, Rodrigo Torrero busca o 'realismo mágico' nas nove canções autorais do álbum 'Erre'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Programado para 6 de novembro, o álbum traz música composta em memória do cachorro do artista.
articles.summary: Programado para 6 de novembro, o álbum traz música composta em memória do cachorro do artista.
articles.body:
Rodrigo Torrero em ilustração exposta na capa do primeiro álbum do artista carioca, 'Erre', produzido por Vinicius Castro — Foto: Arte de Luiz Silva a partir de foto de Aloysio Araripe

♬ Rodrigo Torrero já é nome recorrente no circuito carioca de festivais, no qual vem buscando afirmação como cantor e compositor, com resultados geralmente positivos. Formado em Música pela Unirio, o artista começou a compor em 2013 e, seis anos depois, debutou no mercado fonográfico com a edição do EP “Uma noite de sol” (2019).

Seis singles depois, Torrero chega ao primeiro álbum, “Erre”, programado para 6 de novembro. Antecedido pelos singles que adiantaram as gravações das músicas “Todos os assuntos” e “Mury”, esta uma parceria do compositor com Carol Viani, o álbum “Erre” encadeia nove canções autorais fincadas no território da música que pode ser qualificada como nova MPB , mas com eventuais acenos para o pop.

O álbum foi gravado com produção musical de Vinicius Castro e com participações de artistas e amigos do círculo afetivo do artista. Antonia Medeiros, colega de Torrero na faculdade de música e no grupo vocal Consoantes, figura na música “Pouca vergonha”.

O cantor e compositor carioca Rodrigo Torrero lança em 6 de novembro o primeiro álbum, 'Erre', com participações de colegas do grupo vocal Consoantes — Foto: Aloysio Araripe / Divulgação

Já o canto da faixa “Velha farra” é dividido por Rodrigo Torrero com Guilherme Imia (outro colega da faculdade e do grupo Consoantes) e Tom Rossi, amigo músico dos tempos de escola. A propósito, a música “Velha farra” é homenagem do artista a Totó Joey – cachorro da família morto em 2016 – e se inspira em “Diana” (Toninho Horta e Fernando Brant, 1977), também uma canção escrita em memória de cadela de estimação.

“Errar”, “Ir”, “Julia” e “Mirante” são outras músicas que compõem o repertório inteiramente autoral do álbum “Erre”. São canções situadas em universo caracterizado por Rodrigo Torrero como “realismo mágico”, criado a partir do mix das referências do artista no mundo do realismo fantástico – como a saga de “O senhor dos anéis”– com a magia extraída do cotidiano.

“São canções que abraçam a incerteza do que está do outro lado da curva e que se permitem encantar com o que está ao redor”, filosofa Rodrigo Torrero, torcendo para que o álbum “Erre” configure um acerto na trajetória indie do artista.

articles.title: Rebeca Matta retorna com 'Pélvica', primeiro álbum da artista em 13 anos | G1
articles.body:
Rebeca Matta lança o álbum 'Pélvica' na sexta-feira, 30 de outubro, com dez músicas autorais no repertório in — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Cantora e compositora baiana revelada nos anos 1990, década em que lançou o álbum “Tantas coisas” em 1998, Rebeca Matta retoma a carreira fonográfica e apresenta na sexta-feira, 30 de outubro, o primeiro álbum em 13 anos.

O álbum se chama “Pélvica”, é o quinto da discografia da artista e apresenta dez músicas autorais gravadas com produção musical orquestrada pela própria Rebeca Matta com Guilherme Kastrup e Enio Nogueira. Kastrup toca bateria e percussões em diversas faixas enquanto Nogueira contribui com guitarras, sintetizadores e programação eletrônica.

Carla Suzart assume o contrabaixo no álbum antecedido pelo single “Olho no olho”, editado em 25 de setembro. “Olho no olho” é música gravada por Rebeca com adesões de Chico César, Lan Lanh, Larissa Luz, Mateus Aleluia e Roberto Barreto.

Além de “Olho no olho”, o repertório inédito e autoral do álbum “Pélvica” é composto pelas músicas “Gira”, “Sem perceber”, “O som do silêncio”, “Dentro da minha cabeça”, “Aconchego”, “Me perdoa”, “Sair por aí”, “Ela” e “Danço”.

Sucessor do álbum ao vivo “À flor da pele” (2013) na discografia de Rebeca Matta, o álbum “Pélvica” transita entre MPB, pop e música eletrônica por vias experimentais – marca dessa artista que conseguiu alguma projeção na mídia com o segundo álbum, “Garotas boas vão pro céu, garotas más vão pra qualquer lugar”, editado em 2000.

articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen says 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' is his last in this style of comedy, calling them too risky
articles.summary: Sacha Baron Cohen reveals why "Ali G: Who Iz I?" will be his last over-the-top comedy, citing dangerous stunts and severe dehydration on set.
articles.body: Sacha Baron Cohen is done starring in over-the-top comedies. In a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter, the 55-year-old actor confirmed that his new movie, "Ali G: Who Iz I?," will be his last in the risky, character-driven comedic style that made him famous. "I want to do stuff that challenges me," he told the outlet. "So again, I’m not doing 'Borat 3,' which also would be incredibly challenging. Again, this movie I just did is the most challenging movie I’ve ever done, but I’m not doing more." The actor has said he was done with this style of comedy in the past, but decided to make this movie because he is "terrified of where our society is headed" and thinks of his comedy as a way to comment on it. SACHA BARON COHEN’S RIPPED NEW LOOK FOR MARVEL ROLE HAS FANS DOING A TAKE He explained that through his films, he can "show the extremism on both sides of the political spectrum and the danger of virtuous violence." He added that at the end of the day, he also "wanted to make the funniest film that’s ever been made." "These really are the hardest movies to make, but I suppose I made it because I’m scared of this world of conspiracies and lies that are spread by social media and now by AI," he said. "If we don’t have these shared facts, then democracies crumble, and we can’t have a tolerant society. And to make people laugh is therapy." Cohen's early breakthrough came in 2000, with "Da Ali G Show," and he later gained international recognition with the release of "Borat" in 2006. He followed that up with "Bruno," "The Dictator," "Who is America" and "Borat Subsequent Moviefilm," as well as some dramatic roles in "The Trial of the Chicago 7," "Les Misérables" and "Disclaimer." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Throughout the interview, Cohen explained that these comedies "are dangerous to make" and are "incredibly demanding" on the body, but that he and his crew "try to limit the risks and keep everybody safe." He described the final scene of his latest project as "an eight-hour continuous scene that takes place over 12 locations" with a lot of different elements, filmed as "a continual shot." "There’s gunfire in it. There’s a medical procedure. There are drones, there are explosions, and it’s taking place in the desert," he said. "On the way to shooting it, I bumped into one of the great stuntmen and he said, 'You will go to hospital if you make this movie,' because I explained I’m wearing a prosthetic head in a fat suit. He said, 'You’ll be so dehydrated you’ll be in hospital for two weeks.'" The "Balls Up" star explained that he hired "an endurance specialist who does the Tour de France" to be next to him throughout filming and that, despite the precautions, "a number of people went to the hospital for dehydration." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Despite how it may seem, Cohen assured fans he "will never do a scene if I think I’m actually going to die." "I was about to do a scene [in 'Borat 1'] and we had a cop who had his gun on his thigh and I said, 'Why is your gun on your thigh?' He goes, 'Well, I need to be really fast to draw in this area.' I said, 'Well, how close are you to me?' And he said, 'I’ll be with you within three minutes.' I realized that was not a good thing to do, so I pulled that scene." He also received an acting nomination for his role in "The Trial of the Chicago 7."

articles.body: Marvel Studios’ highly anticipated ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ has reportedly crossed the USD 125 million mark in advance ticket sales months before its theatrical release. This has reportedly set a new benchmark for presales, and has reportedly put the upcoming superhero blockbuster well ahead of ‘Dune: Part Three’ in early sales projections.The latest figures mark a significant boost in box office numbers from the USD 100 million milestone it hit early this month, as reported Global Box Office. The latest development comes shortly after Marvel released a new trailer for ‘Avengers: Doomsday’, featuring Chris Hemsworth’s Thor warning the assembled superheroes about the threat posed by Robert Downey Jr's Doctor Doom. “Doom will tear this world apart… team up, stand together,” Thor says in the trailer, which has further fuelled anticipation for the film.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ presales surge ahead of releaseThe film’s advance ticket sales began unusually early, with premium-format tickets going on sale on July 20. The early start has given the film a substantial lead over films that began selling tickets closer to their release dates.Global Box Office has projected a domestic opening weekend estimated between USD 300 million and a potential USD 400 million opening.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ vs ‘Dune: Part Three’: A ‘Dunesday’ box office battleWith both ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ and ‘Dune: Part Three’ scheduled to open on December 18, the clash dubbed ‘Dunesday’ has already tipped the scales in 'Avengers' favour. Early tracking estimates suggest that ‘Doomsday’ could deliver an opening weekend approximately three to four times bigger than that of ‘Dune: Part Three’.Denis Villeneuve’s ‘Dune: Part Three’ has also generated strong demand for premium-format screenings, with the film beating 'The Odyssey' to now hold the record for the highest first-day presales record at London’s BFI IMAX.IMAX dispute adds another dimension to the box office clashWhile 'Dune' has blocked all IMAX screens, 'Doomsday' has taken over Infinity Vision and other premium large-format screens. articles.summary: SS Rajamouli is known not only for his grand filmmaking but also for his extensive promotional strategies.
articles.body: SS Rajamouli is known not only for his grand filmmaking but also for his extensive promotional strategies. His 2022 film ‘RRR’, starring Jr NTR and Ram Charan, received global acclaim and went on to become an international sensation. Now, Varun Gupta, who was involved in the film’s marketing campaign, has revealed how Rajamouli and his son, SS Karthikeya, kept him on his toes throughout the process.Speaking on the Everyday Empires Podcast, Gupta recalled the challenges of promoting the film, especially in the Hindi-speaking markets, where audiences were not always able to distinguish between the two lead actors.Why ‘RRR’ used the ‘Baahubali’ logoGupta explained that the team wanted to use Rajamouli’s previous success, ‘Baahubali’, to build awareness about ‘RRR’. However, instead of writing the film’s title in text, they used its logo on the posters.“When we were doing RRR, people couldn’t differentiate between the two heroes in the Hindi belts, but it was the case where the director’s previous film was a very big hit in the Hindi belts — Baahubali. So, in the poster, we made sure there was a line ‘from the director of’, and we didn’t write Baahubali. We put the logo of Baahubali. Because subconsciously, you will always recall the logo of the film, not the typography of the film,” Gupta said.Rajamouli and Karthikeya trusted the marketing teamGupta also revealed that Rajamouli and Karthikeya were closely involved in the film’s marketing decisions. He said they trusted the team’s ideas and often approved its suggestions without questioning them.“In RRR, the two people, SS Rajamouli and his son Karthikeya, were heading the entire decision-making of marketing. They really believed in us. If we were saying, ‘This is how we should do it,’ they said, ‘Okay, done.’ No questions asked. And that’s when I was like, they are not even questioning. We need to be even more cautious and accountable,” he said.Gupta said the trust placed in him made him more careful about every marketing decision. He recalled that Rajamouli and Karthikeya gave him sleepless nights, but clarified that it was in a positive way.“They are the ones who have given me sleepless nights,” Gupta said, adding that it was “in the right way” and that “They kept me on my toes.”According to trade analyst Sacnilk, ‘RRR’ went on to collect around Rs 1,230 crore worldwide during its theatrical run.SS Rajamouli’s next filmMeanwhile, Rajamouli is preparing for his next globetrotter film, ‘Varanasi’, starring Mahesh Babu and Priyanka Chopra Jonas. articles.title: Vedika Pinto: I’m still processing all that Musafir Cafe has brought my way
articles.summary: In Musafir Cafe, Vedika Pinto plays Sudha, a divorce lawyer who chooses her career over love.
articles.body: In Musafir Cafe, Vedika Pinto plays Sudha, a divorce lawyer who chooses her career over love. Based on Divya Prakash Dubey’s novel of the same name, the series has sparked debate over Sudha’s choices, with viewers split between admiration and criticism. But the polarising character has also won the actress a growing fanbase. Vedika shares she has barely had time to take in what the show has done for her.‘I feel like I inherently understand Sudha’When asked how she’ll take Sudha into Season 2, Vedika says she can’t say for sure, as shooting for the new season hasn’t begun. “I’m both nervous and excited to see how I find my way back to Sudha. Of course, there was a lot of work involved in building the character the first time around, from understanding where she came from to discovering the little personality traits and circumstantial nuances that made her who she is. But I also feel like I inherently understand her, and in some ways, she has become a part of me.” She adds,“I’m hoping that makes it easier to tap into her, but I think it’s a question I’ll be better equipped to answer once I’m actually back on set and have had the chance to step into her shoes again.”‘I’m still just going through the motions!' Vedika played a lead role in Anurag Kashyap’s Nishaanchi, but it was Musafir Cafe that made her a household name. “Honestly, the pace of my life has picked up so dramatically since the release of Musafir Cafe that I feel like I’m still just going through the motions! I don’t think I’ve had the chance to zoom out and really process or analyse all the changes yet. I’m overwhelmed, grateful, motivated and excited, all at once. So many doors are opening, and dreams that I’ve held on to for so long are beginning to feel like they’re finally being actualised. It’s an incredible feeling, and I’m just so ready to embrace everything that comes my way,” she says.Drawing your curtains and seeing the mountains right in front of you was extraordinaryMusafir Cafe was largely filmed in Mussoorie and Bhopal and is full of shots of the mountains. On shooting in the hills, Vedika says, “There’s something quite extraordinary about waking up in the morning, drawing your curtains and seeing the mountains right in front of you. You feel so small in the grand scheme of things, and yet, strangely, so invincible at the same time. It’s incredibly humbling and grounding, and I absolutely loved that experience.” The location also made the work harder. “Of course, shooting in the hills comes with its challenges. It can get freezing, sometimes you have to trek to reach your locations, and early-morning shoots can be quite demanding. But when you’re actually there, immersed in the world you’re creating, you don’t really think about any of that.”‘I started out wanting to work exclusively in films’Vedika has worked across films and streaming, and it was OTT that made her a familiar face. She shares,“As an actor, what draws me in the most is the story. Everything else is secondary. Although, I won’t lie, I started out wanting to work exclusively in films. You grow up watching movies on the big screen, and that’s where the dream of becoming an actor really begins.” The dream has not faded, even as the series opens other doors. “It’s quite surreal that Musafir Cafe has brought me so much of the recognition I’d hoped for and opened up so many new avenues for me. I still dream of doing films, but I don’t think the platform itself matters as much as the story being told.”Ultimately, I’m excited to explore different formats and see where the stories take meGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
